title: 17. Perimeter and Areas of Plane Figures

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
q.e: A triangle is half of a rectangle on the same base and height: ½ × 10 × 6.

q.t: Use Heron’s formula to find the area of a triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 cm.
Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 4 cm.
A rectangle is 12 cm by 5 cm. Find its diagonal.
q.e: The diagonal is the hypotenuse: √(144 + 25).

q.t: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 8 cm. Find its area.
q.e: The diagonals cut it into 4 right triangles, which together make half the 10 × 8 rectangle.

q.t: A trapezium has parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Average of the parallel sides × height: 10 × 5.

q.t: A square has perimeter 40 cm. Find its area.
A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 4 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Cut off a triangle from one end and move it to the other: it becomes a 9 × 4 rectangle.

q.t: A right triangle has legs 7 cm and 24 cm. Find its area.
q.e: The legs are base and height: ½ × 7 × 24.

q.t: Find the semi-perimeter of a triangle with sides 7, 8 and 9 cm.
q.e: Half of 7 + 8 + 9.

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with sides 13, 14 and 15 cm.
An isosceles triangle has equal sides 10 cm and base 12 cm. Find its area.
q.e: The height bisects the base: √(100 − 36) = 8. Area = ½ × 12 × 8.

q.t: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 18 cm. Find its area.
A rhombus has side 10 cm and one diagonal 12 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Half-diagonals are at right angles: √(100 − 36) = 8, so the other diagonal is 16. ½ × 12 × 16.

q.t: A square has diagonal 10 cm. Find its area.
q.e: A square is a rhombus, so area = ½ × d × d = ½ × 100.

q.t: A rectangle has perimeter 46 cm and diagonal 17 cm. Find its area.
A 20 m × 10 m garden has a 2 m wide path all round it outside. Find the area of the path.
q.e: Outer rectangle 24 × 14 = 336, minus the garden 200.

q.t: A trapezium has area 90 cm² and parallel sides 8 cm and 10 cm. Find its height.
An equilateral triangle has height 6√3 cm. Find its side.
q.e: Height = (√3/2) × side.

q.t: A square field has area 400 m². Fencing costs ₹15 per metre. Find the cost (in ₹).
q.e: Side 20 m, perimeter 80 m: 80 × 15.

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with sides 25, 39 and 56 cm.
An equilateral triangle has area 49√3 cm². Find its perimeter.
A trapezium has parallel sides 20 cm and 6 cm and non-parallel sides 13 cm and 15 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Slide one slanting side across to make a triangle with sides 14, 13, 15 (area 84). Its height on 14 is 12 — the trapezium’s height. ½ × 26 × 12.

q.t: A rhombus has perimeter 52 cm and one diagonal 24 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Side 13, half-diagonal 12, so the other half-diagonal is 5. ½ × 24 × 10.

q.t: A 60 m × 40 m park has two 3 m wide roads crossing through its middle, one parallel to each side. Find the road area.
q.e: 3 × 60 + 3 × 40, but the 3 × 3 crossing was counted twice.

q.t: A rectangular field has sides in the ratio 3 : 2 and perimeter 100 m. Find its area.
q.e: l + b = 50, split 3 : 2 gives 30 and 20.

q.t: A square has diagonal 12√2 cm. Find its area.
q.e: The diagonal of a square is side × √2, so the side is 12.

q.t: An isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse 10√2 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Each leg is 10 (hypotenuse = leg × √2). ½ × 10 × 10.

q.t: A triangle’s sides are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its area.
q.e: Sides 9, 12, 15 — a right triangle (3-4-5 scaled by 3). ½ × 9 × 12.

q.t: Find the area of a regular hexagon of side 6 cm.
q.e: It splits into 6 equilateral triangles of side 6, each (√3/4) × 36 = 9√3.

q.t: Find the area of a triangle with sides 17, 25 and 28 cm.
A triangle has sides 17, 25 and 28 cm. Find its height to the longest side.
q.e: Area 210 = ½ × 28 × h.

q.t: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 5, BC = 12, CD = 14, DA = 15 cm and ∠ABC = 90°. Find its area.
q.e: AC = 13 (5-12-13). ΔABC = 30. ΔACD has sides 13, 14, 15: area 84.

q.t: A rhombus-shaped field has side 30 m and one diagonal 48 m. It is shared equally by 18 cows to graze. How much does each cow get?
q.e: Half-diagonal 24 gives the other half 18, so the diagonals are 48 and 36. Area 864 ÷ 18.

q.t: An equilateral triangle has height h. Its area is…
q.e: Side = 2h/√3. Area = ½ × (2h/√3) × h = h²/√3.

q.t: An 80 m × 60 m lawn has a 5 m wide path inside it along all four edges. Find the area of the path.
q.e: The part inside the path is 70 × 50 = 3500. 4800 − 3500.

q.t: A triangle has perimeter 42 cm and two sides 13 cm and 14 cm. Find its area.
q.e: The third side is 15, s = 21: √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6).

q.t: An equilateral triangle and a square have the same perimeter. Find area of triangle : area of square.
q.e: Square side a gives triangle side 4a/3. (√3/4)(16a²/9) ÷ a² = 4√3/9.

q.t: Each side of a triangle is doubled. By what percent does its area increase?
q.e: Area scales with side², so it becomes 4 times — an increase of 3 times the original.

q.t: A rectangle’s length is increased by 20% and its breadth decreased by 20%. By what percent does its area decrease?
q.e: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so the area is 96% of what it was.
